content.title: About
content.content: Crimini mushrooms (Agaricus bisporus) are medium‑sized brown‑gray caps that are a more mature form of the common white button mushroom. They have a firm, meaty texture and a slightly nutty aroma, making them a popular choice for a wide range of dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crimini are the intermediate stage between white button and portobello mushrooms, with a darker, denser cap.
When exposed to ultraviolet light, mushrooms can produce vitamin D2.
Commercial crimini are grown in controlled indoor farms, allowing year‑round supply.
They contain about 3 g of protein per 100 g, higher than most vegetables.
Mushrooms can accumulate certain heavy metals from the substrate, so sourcing from reputable growers is important.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Crimini provide niacin (B3), riboflavin (B2) and pyridoxine (B6), which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A 100‑g serving contains only about 22 kcal, making them ideal for weight‑conscious diets.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Selenium and various polyphenols in crimini help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Beta‑glucans in the mushroom cell walls can enhance the activity of immune cells.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes a healthy gut microbiome and aids digestion.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mushrooms, ranging from skin rashes to respiratory symptoms.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Mushrooms contain purines, which can raise uric acid levels in people prone to gout.

items.title: Spoilage risk
items.content: If stored in high humidity, crimini can develop mold that produces mycotoxins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crimini mushrooms can be eaten raw in salads, sautéed, roasted, grilled, or added to soups, stews, and sauces. Before cooking, gently wipe the caps to remove any debris and trim the stems if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store crimini in a paper bag in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. They stay fresh for 3‑5 days. Avoid airtight plastic containers, which trap moisture and accelerate spoilage.
